claims.summary: Top-level SoC integration module that connects a CPU core to an I/O network slot via a bidirectional event-driven drive interface.
claims.subject: arm_soc_top
claims.explanation: The module instantiates a cpu_slot and an IONet_slot, connected by two event_drive signals (w_driveFrmCPU, w_driveToCPU). No data or event ports are exposed at the top level, suggesting this is an internal SoC fabric node rather than a chip boundary module. The only top-level control input is initMode_pad, used as a condition.

claims.summary: Routes event-driven drive signals between the CPU slot and the I/O network slot, forming a bidirectional control handshake.
claims.subject: CPU-to-IO event drive bridge
claims.explanation: The two key_component_connections show a direct event_drive loop: u_cpu.o_driveToMesh drives io_slot.i_drvFCPU via w_driveFrmCPU, and io_slot.o_drv2CPU drives u_cpu.i_driveFromMesh via w_driveToCPU. No other data or event paths are present, indicating this module is a simple bridge for CPU-I/O drive coordination.

claims.subject: u_cpu (cpu_slot)
claims.summary: CPU core slot that generates drive commands to the I/O network and receives drive responses from it.
claims.explanation: u_cpu outputs w_driveFrmCPU (event_drive to io_slot) and inputs w_driveToCPU (event_drive from io_slot). No data ports are listed, suggesting this is a control-only interface for drive handshaking.

claims.subject: io_slot (IONet_slot)
claims.summary: I/O network slot that receives CPU drive commands and returns drive responses, with a GPIO data output.
claims.explanation: io_slot inputs w_driveFrmCPU (event_drive from u_cpu) and outputs w_driveToCPU (event_drive to u_cpu). It also has a gpio_data_o output, indicating it can produce data to external GPIO pads, though no top-level data output is exposed in this module.
